packs.title: Tracks, Trails & Small Wonders
packs.promise: Follow railway tools, a science question, living collections and short views above the valley.

q.s: Find the smaller things behind a railway.
st: Enter the museum by its signed visitor route. Choose three actual objects that tell different parts of a journey: moving, communicating and keeping people or equipment ready.
Read the labels for the purpose of each. Use a different object if a display is closed; you do not need to enter a locomotive cab or touch equipment.
Write a three-object journey in your own words, explaining how each object helps the next stage.

q.s: Make a small study on a short hill walk.
st: From the public Horse Gulch trailhead, follow the signed shared lower road on foot. Walk uphill for up to 20 minutes at a comfortable pace, then choose a safe stop off the moving line; turn sooner if needed.
Notice four textures in view: ground, plant, rock and sky. Make four original marks or four short phrases without collecting anything or leaving the trail.
Return by the same road, allowing at least your outward walking time plus rest. Title your four-part study after reaching the trailhead.

q.t: Three Ways to Read a Work
q.s: Connect a maker, a material and a place.
st: Visit during an ordinary open weekday with lawful campus parking or onward transport arranged. Choose one actual displayed work or object that has interpretation you can read.
Collect three labelled connections: maker or community where stated, material, and a place or region. Mark any missing detail as unknown; do not invent a cultural meaning.
Write one original question that the work leaves you with. Your notes are enough; follow the gallery’s current photo rules.

packs.title: Main Avenue in Layers
packs.promise: Read a few downtown blocks through brick, makers, books and small original responses.

q.s: Make a tiny study of an everyday doorway.
st: Find an ordinary sidewalk position opposite or beside these storefronts, using a marked crossing if needed.
Notice a horizontal line, a vertical line, a repeated shape and a recessed entrance or window relationship.
Make four original lines or four short phrases. Keep moving if the pavement becomes busy; a doorway is not a seat or sketching platform.

q.s: Let a display start a flavor idea.
st: During an open visitor period, choose three actual display or package details: a shape, an ingredient word and a color.
Write one playful description of each without opening, sampling or handling food. Use only what the label actually states.
Invent a one-sentence name for a fictional chocolate inspired by your own day. Keep it separate from any real product or ingredient promise.

q.t: A Shelf for the Next Journey
st: Find three actual books from different shelves that suggest different kinds of journey: a real place, an imagined world and a new skill or idea.
Read a short description or contents information available for browsing. Note a reason each belongs in your trio; do not photograph or copy pages.
Choose which you would open first and write an original one-line explanation. Put any handled book back as the shop requests.
